modules.title: Iridoid / nepetalactol / nepetalactone pathway

records.name: (6E)-8-Hydroxygeraniol
records.note: Defined E,E diol reference; also called 10-hydroxygeraniol under alternative numbering.

records.name: (6E)-8-Oxogeranial
records.note: Defined E,E dialdehyde substrate for ISY; also called 10-oxogeranial under alternative numbering.

records.name: cis-trans-Nepetalactol
records.note: The selected record assigns 4aS,7S,7aR. C1 anomeric configuration is unassigned; this is not one fully specified lactol anomer.

records.name: cis-cis-Nepetalactol
records.note: The selected record assigns 4aR,7S,7aS. C1 anomeric configuration is unassigned; this is not one fully specified lactol anomer.

records.name: cis-trans-Nepetalactone
records.note: Defined 4aS,7S,7aR lactone reference; oxidation of the matching lactol removes its anomeric centre.

records.name: cis-cis-Nepetalactone
records.note: Defined 4aR,7S,7aS lactone reference.

edges.label: CrG8O / CYP76B6 · hydroxylation
edges.detail: Characterised Catharanthus roseus early iridoid chemistry. G8O can also perform further oxidation.

edges.label: Cr8-HGO · two oxidations · NAD+
edges.detail: Condenses two alcohol oxidations. Cr8-HGO accepts 8-hydroxygeraniol and the mono-oxidised intermediates with NAD+.

edges.label: ISY + NmNEPS2 · tested cascade
edges.detail: ISY first reduces the substrate to a reactive enol; NmNEPS2 promotes cis-trans cyclisation. Tested combinations include CrISY and NmISY2.

edges.label: ISY + NmNEPS3 · tested cascade
edges.detail: Reduction and subsequent stereoselective cyclisation are distinct activities. NmNEPS3 forms the 7S cis-cis product.

edges.label: NmNEPS1 · lactol oxidation · NAD+
edges.detail: NAD+-dependent oxidation of the matching lactol to its lactone.

edges.label: NmNEPS1 · lactol oxidation · NAD+
edges.detail: NmNEPS1 oxidises both displayed lactol stereoisomers while retaining their assigned core stereochemistry.

modules.scopeNote: Reference reconstruction combining characterised Catharanthus early enzymes with tested ISY/Nepeta NEPS cascades; not one demonstrated native organism's complete route.

enzymes.name: Iridoid synthase
enzymes.activity: Reductive activation to a reactive enol

enzymes.name: cis-trans-Nepetalactol synthase
cofactors: Bound NAD+; no redox turnover in cyclisation

enzymes.name: cis-cis-Nepetalactol synthase
cofactors: Bound NAD+; no redox turnover in cyclisation

enzymes.name: Nepetalactol dehydrogenase
enzymes.activity: Lactol oxidation; also has cis-trans cyclase activity

suggestedReactionCards.answerConcept: Reduction followed by cyclisation; a multi-enzyme cascade
Lactol oxidation to lactone with NAD+

modules.title: Artemisinin precursor branch

records.name: (+)-Artemisinic alcohol
records.note: Primary allylic alcohol formed by C12 oxidation of amorpha-4,11-diene.

records.name: Artemisinic aldehyde
records.note: Branch-point aldehyde: DBR2 reduces its 11(13) double bond; further oxidation instead yields artemisinic acid.

records.name: (+)-Artemisinic acid
records.note: Unsaturated acid branch product. Do not depict DBR2 reducing this acid directly to DHAA.

records.name: (11R)-Dihydroartemisinic aldehyde
records.note: Stereochemically defined DBR2 product with a saturated 11(13) bond.

records.name: (11R)-Dihydroartemisinic acid
records.note: Defined natural-pathway DHAA reference; the selected PubChem structure assigns the side-chain acid centre as 2R.

edges.label: AaCYP71AV1 + CPR · C12 hydroxylation
edges.detail: Characterised Artemisia annua P450 chemistry; redox partner supplies electrons.

edges.label: AaCYP71AV1 + CPR · oxidation
edges.detail: CYP71AV1 supports sequential C12 oxidation in engineered yeast. AaADH1 provides an additional characterised alcohol-oxidation route.

edges.label: AaCYP71AV1 / AaALDH1 · acid branch
edges.detail: Alternative enzymes can oxidise this aldehyde to the unsaturated acid; this is a branch competing with aldehyde reduction.

edges.label: AaDBR2 · 11(13) reduction · NADPH
edges.detail: DBR2 is an enoate reductase acting on the unsaturated aldehyde, not a direct artemisinic-acid-to-DHAA enzyme.

edges.label: AaALDH1 · aldehyde oxidation
edges.detail: Recombinant AaALDH1 catalyses NAD(P)+-dependent oxidation of the dihydro aldehyde to its acid.

edges.label: O2-driven autoxidation · several stages
edges.detail: Experimentally demonstrated nonenzymatic oxidative chemistry via peroxide intermediates. This condensed connection is not a single characterised enzyme reaction.

modules.scopeNote: Characterised Artemisia oxidation/reduction stages followed by separately labelled nonenzymatic oxidative chemistry.

suggestedReactionCards.answerConcept: Alkene reduction; the aldehyde remains an aldehyde

records.name: ent-Kaurenol
records.note: The C19 alcohol intermediate in the characterised plant ent-kaurene oxidase sequence. Use this fully specified reference, not a generic kaurenol isomer.

records.name: ent-Kaurenal
records.note: The aldehyde intermediate in the plant KO sequence. ChEBI also lists the equivalent parent-system name kaur-16-en-18-al.

records.name: ent-Kaurenoic acid
records.note: The carboxylic-acid product of plant KO and substrate for plant KAO. Neutral-acid structure is shown.

records.name: ent-7α-Hydroxykaurenoic acid
records.note: Use the exact ChEBI stereostructure. The names ent-7α-hydroxykaurenoic acid and (-)-kaur-16-en-7β-ol-19-oic acid occur for this reference structure; changing the placement of the ent prefix changes how alpha/beta descriptions are interpreted. A PubChem CID was not independently verified.

records.name: Gibberellin A12 aldehyde
records.note: A C20 gibberellin intermediate formed after KAO-catalysed ring-B contraction. Neutral-acid form is shown.

records.name: Gibberellin A12
records.note: The C20 gibberellin product of the plant KO/KAO sequence. This is a reference pathway, not a functional assignment to an untested Tinospora enzyme.

enzymes.name: ent-Kaurene oxidase
cofactors: NADPH via a compatible P450 reductase
enzymes.note: The Arabidopsis gene name GA3 refers to the KO gene here, not the molecule gibberellin A3.

enzymes.name: ent-Kaurenoic acid oxidase
cofactors: NADPH via a compatible P450 reductase
enzymes.note: Both Arabidopsis CYP88A enzymes were characterised in yeast as catalysing the three KAO stages.

edges.label: AtKO1 / CYP701A3 · oxidation
edges.detail: First C19 oxidation in the characterised plant KO sequence.

edges.label: AtKO1 / CYP701A3 · oxidation
edges.detail: KO oxidises the alcohol intermediate to the aldehyde. This is a net biochemical stage, not an elementary single-electron mechanism.

edges.label: AtKO1 / CYP701A3 · oxidation
edges.detail: Further KO-catalysed oxidation produces ent-kaurenoic acid.

edges.label: AtKAO1/2 · hydroxylation
edges.detail: First stage of the characterised plant CYP88A/KAO sequence.

edges.label: AtKAO1/2 · ring-B contraction
edges.detail: The second KAO stage contracts ring B and generates the gibbane skeleton. The detailed rearrangement is distinct from the earlier class II labdane/halimane/clerodane cascade.

edges.label: AtKAO1/2 · aldehyde oxidation
edges.detail: The third KAO stage oxidises the remaining aldehyde to a carboxylic acid.

modules.title: Carotenoid cleavage toward ABA

records.name: 9-cis-Violaxanthin
records.note: A specifically defined NCED substrate. Do not substitute the all-trans violaxanthin record.

records.name: 2-cis,4-trans-Xanthoxin
records.note: A C15 apocarotenoid produced by cleavage of a C40 carotenoid. It is not a C40 skeleton or a direct FPP-cyclase product.

records.name: (+)-Abscisic aldehyde
records.note: The (2Z,4E),(1S) reference aldehyde. Do not replace it with 2-trans-(+)-abscisic aldehyde or the opposite enantiomer.

records.name: (+)-Abscisic acid
records.note: Natural (+)-(1′S,2Z,4E)-ABA, represented as the neutral acid. PubChem CID5702609 is a trans,trans geometry record and is not this selected product.

enzymes.name: 9-cis-Epoxycarotenoid dioxygenase
enzymes.note: The illustrated cleavage uses a maize reference enzyme. NCED also acts on 9′-cis-neoxanthin; all-trans counterparts are not equivalent substrates.

enzymes.name: Xanthoxin dehydrogenase
enzymes.note: The characterised net conversion includes alcohol oxidation and epoxide rearrangement. Proposed internal chemical ordering should not be presented as separately isolated intermediates.

enzymes.name: Abscisic aldehyde oxidase
enzymes.note: AAO3 was characterised as catalysing the final ABA biosynthesis stage in Arabidopsis leaves. ABA3 activates the molybdenum cofactor; ABA3 is not the aldehyde-oxidising enzyme.

edges.label: Geometric-isomer relationship
edges.detail: Relates the reference violaxanthin drawing to the specifically required 9-cis substrate. This link does not assign an isomerisation enzyme.

edges.label: NCED / VP14 · oxidative cleavage
edges.detail: A C40 carotenoid is cleaved into C15 xanthoxin and a C25 apo-aldehyde. The coproduct must remain visible in the reaction annotation: 40 = 15 + 25.

edges.label: ABA2 · NAD+-dependent conversion
edges.detail: Characterised conversion of xanthoxin to abscisic aldehyde. The net reaction oxidises the 4′-hydroxyl to a ketone and rearranges the epoxide to the unsaturated hydroxy ring.

edges.label: AAO3 · aldehyde oxidation
edges.detail: Aldehyde oxidation gives natural (+)-ABA. This is an aldehyde-oxidase reference stage, not a P450/CPR reaction.

modules.scopeNote: Maize VP14 and Arabidopsis ABA2/AAO3 are reference enzyme examples from different species. This map does not imply a tested three-enzyme reconstruction or assign functions to Tinospora candidates.

modules.title: Plant poly-cis carotenoid route

records.name: 15,9′-di-cis-Phytofluene
records.note: A defined poly-cis intermediate of the plant PDS route. Distinct from the all-trans phytofluene reference.

records.name: 9,15,9′-tri-cis-ζ-Carotene
records.note: PDS product and Z-ISO substrate; its central 15-cis bond is explicit.

records.name: 9,9′-di-cis-ζ-Carotene
records.note: Z-ISO product and ZDS substrate. Its central double bond is trans; the 9/9′ bonds remain cis. Distinct from existing all-trans ζ-carotene CID5280788.

records.name: 7,9,9′-tri-cis-Neurosporene
records.note: Defined ZDS intermediate. ChEBI-linked structure; PubChem CID intentionally unassigned because its cross-reference was not verified directly.

records.name: Prolycopene · tetra-cis-Lycopene
records.note: 7,9,7′,9′-tetra-cis-lycopene, the CRTISO substrate.

edges.label: PDS · first desaturation
edges.detail: Plant-type PDS uses plastoquinone as an electron acceptor. This route retains explicitly assigned cis geometry.

edges.label: PDS · second desaturation
edges.detail: The second PDS desaturation produces tri-cis ζ-carotene.

edges.label: Z-ISO · central cis → trans
edges.detail: Z-ISO isomerises the central 15–15′ bond. Light can photoisomerise this bond in suitable conditions; that is a distinct physical process.

edges.label: ZDS · first desaturation
edges.detail: ZDS processes the appropriate geometric substrate using a quinone electron acceptor.

edges.label: ZDS · second desaturation
edges.detail: The second ZDS desaturation gives tetra-cis lycopene.

edges.label: CRTISO · cis → trans
edges.detail: CRTISO converts the poly-cis product toward all-trans lycopene. It uses reduced FAD for a non-redox isomerisation.

modules.scope: A separate plant poly-cis lane. Keep the existing bacterial/fungal CrtI reference lane separate.

modules.title: Astaxanthin esterification and analytical hydrolysis

records.name: Astaxanthin monopalmitate · structural model
records.validation: Derived by acylating one OH of the supplied existing astaxanthin structure; RDKit formula/CIP validation remains pending.
records.note: Representative palmitate ester retaining the chosen parent stereochemistry. It is not a claimed identity for a rac/meso analytical standard or a specific ScDGAT2-1 product.

records.name: Astaxanthin dipalmitate
records.note: This CID represents a computed stereochemically defined structure. Its depositor synonym list also contains rac/meso mixture names; those synonyms must not redefine the illustrated stereoisomer.
records.validation: SMILES and formula copied from PubChem; runtime validation pending.

edges.label: One OH acylated · reference example
edges.detail: Shows esterification chemistry with a representative palmitoyl group. Characterised xanthophyll acyltransferases support the reaction class; this illustration does not establish exact donor specificity for any named enzyme.

edges.label: Second OH acylated · reference example
edges.detail: Both astaxanthin hydroxyl groups are esterified in this structural comparison. The C40 carotenoid core remains despite the larger total carbon count.

edges.label: Cholesterol esterase · analytical hydrolysis
edges.detail: An in-vitro analytical treatment that releases free astaxanthin and fatty acid. It is not a native export reaction.

edges.label: De-esterification · two ester bonds
edges.detail: Condenses hydrolysis of both ester bonds during analytical de-esterification; it does not claim a one-step native conversion.

enzymeExamples.name: ScDGAT2-1
enzymeExamples.evidence: Characterised bifunctional DGAT associated with astaxanthin ester biosynthesis; the original study reports astaxanthin-DHA monoester and lipid-droplet deposition.
enzymeExamples.scope: Do not relabel palmitate models as its experimentally proven products.

enzymeExamples.name: HpDGAT1
enzymeExamples.evidence: Recombinant protein enhanced xanthophyll ester formation in ER-membrane assays and an engineered E. coli system.
enzymeExamples.scope: Retain the assay context; avoid claiming unrestricted acyl-donor specificity.

enzymeExamples.name: Cholesterol esterase
enzymeExamples.evidence: Analytical enzymolysis of extracted H. pluvialis esters.
enzymeExamples.scope: The study used acetone/Tris buffer, pH7, 37°C; its starting analytical condition used 2 U enzyme and 0.75 h. These are study conditions, not a universal protocol.

modules.transportScope: Track chemical form, storage and extracellular recovery separately. Improved export in engineered yeast is an untested hypothesis.

qualifications: Early iridoid steps use characterised Catharanthus roseus enzymes; lactol/lactone branching uses tested Nepeta mussinii enzyme systems.
The composite iridoid map is a reconstructed reference route, not proof that all displayed enzymes co-occur in one native organism.
No Tinospora enzyme or product assignments are made.
Do not add a stable neutral enol molecule to the catalogue.
Do not equate the two-word nepetalactol stereochemical labels with the clerodane naming convention.
Do not label DHAA-to-artemisinin as an enzyme step.
All image fields are null: no RDKit assets were generated and no SMILES were computationally parsed in this environment.
Use ChEBI29611 for the fully specified ent-kaurenol reference. ChEBI15416 currently presents an InChI with one unspecified stereocentre despite similar displayed SMILES.
ChEBI15419 is the verified structure for the selected hydroxykaurenoic-acid intermediate. Alpha/beta text alone is unsafe when the placement of the ent prefix differs.
Existing neoxanthin must not be assumed to be the NCED-compatible 9′-cis structure. The compact route uses independently defined 9-cis-violaxanthin.
ABA-derived C15 records require explicit apocarotenoid family support; do not silently classify them as ordinary FPP-derived sesquiterpenoids or C40 skeletons.
No files or illustrations were generated because the execution environment is unavailable.
All copied SMILES require RDKit parsing, formula and stereochemical checks before integration.
The monopalmitate is a labelled structural model with no assigned PubChem CID.
Do not substitute existing all-trans phytofluene, ζ-carotene or neurosporene records for the poly-cis plant intermediates.
Do not model esterification/hydrolysis as one reversible native enzyme reaction.
